# Deep-URI device ID case sensitivity (2026-01-24 19:34Z)

_**User**_

when trying to open a deep-uri like "miataru://Amsterdam_nl" the deviceID is converted to uppercase only. 

But this is wrong as the deviceIDs are actually case sensitive. Why is that

---

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_


Investigating why deviceIDs are uppercased in deep links. Searching for deep link handling code.

        "contents": "    private func handleIncomingURL(_ url: URL) {\n        guard url.scheme == \"miataru\" else { return }\n        let deviceID = (url.host ?? \"\").uppercased()\n        guard !deviceID.isEmpty else { return }\n\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            // When resuming from background, SwiftUI may restore navigation state after the URL\n            // event is delivered. Deferring slightly ensures the deep link wins over restoration.\n            await Task.yield()\n            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 180_000_000)\n\n            // If the device already exists, navigate to it; otherwise fall back to add flow.\n            if KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.contains(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {\n                showAddDeviceSheet = false\n                pendingDeviceID = nil\n                SettingsManager.shared.lastOpenedDeviceID = deviceID\n            } else {\n                pendingDeviceID = deviceID\n                showAddDeviceSheet = true\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nprivate struct DeviceWindowEntrypoint: View {\n    @Binding var deviceID: String?\n    @Environment(\\.openWindow) private var openWindow\n    @Environment(\\.dismissWindow) private var dismissWindow\n\n    init(deviceID: Binding&lt;String?&gt;) {\n        self._deviceID = deviceID\n    }\n\n    var body: some View {\n        Group {\n            if let id = deviceID {\n                iPad_DeviceMapView(deviceID: id, shouldUpdateLastOpenedDeviceID: false)\n            } else {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"no_device_selected\", comment: \"No device selected for this window.\"))\n            }\n        }\n        .task {\n            if LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation {\n                LaunchGuard.isFirstActivation = false\n                openWindow(id: \"main\")\n                if let id = deviceID {\n                    dismissWindow(value: id)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * SharedWidgetConfig.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 2026-01-06.\n */\n\nimport Foundation\n\nstruct SharedWidgetConfig: Codable {\n    let miataruServerURL: String\n    let deviceIDs: [String]\n    let ownDeviceID: String?\n    let authorizationToken: String?\n}\n\nenum SharedWidgetConfigManager {\n    private static let configFileName = \"SharedWidgetConfig.json\"\n    private static let appGroupIdentifier = \"group.com.miataru.ios\"\n\n    static var sharedContainerURL: URL? {\n        FileManager.default.containerURL(forSecurityApplicationGroupIdentifier: appGroupIdentifier)\n    }\n\n    static var configURL: URL? {\n        sharedContainerURL?.appendingPathComponent(configFileName)\n    }\n\n    static func write(_ config: SharedWidgetConfig) {\n        guard let url = configURL else { return }\n        do {\n            let data = try JSONEncoder().encode(config)\n            try data.write(to: url, options: [.atomic])\n        } catch {\n            print(\"Failed to write shared widget config: \\(error)\")\n        }\n    }\n\n    static func read() -&gt; SharedWidgetConfig? {\n        guard let url = configURL else { return nil }\n        guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else { return nil }\n        do {\n            return try JSONDecoder().decode(SharedWidgetConfig.self, from: data)\n        } catch {\n            print(\"Failed to decode shared widget config: \\(error)\")\n            return nil\n        }\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "- Stores &amp; caches:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving to Application Support)\n  - &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; (last locations + reverse geocode queue)\n  - &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; (cached &#96;MKRoute&#96; by device &amp; transport; distance-based validity)\n- Utilities:\n  - &#96;thisDeviceIDManager&#96; (device ID generation + legacy migration)\n  - &#96;Haptic&#96; (success/warning/error feedback)\n\n### Key Dependencies\n- **CodeScanner**: QR code scanning functionality\n- **MiataruAPIClient** (via local &#96;Libraries/MiataruClientSwift&#96;): Miataru protocol client\n- **QRCode**: QR code generation\n- **SwiftImageReadWrite**: Image handling utilities\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n### Code Organization\n- **Views**: Keep UI logic minimal, delegate to managers\n- **Managers**: Handle business logic and data persistence\n- **Models**: Use SwiftUI's built-in data binding\n- **Assets**: Organize by platform and feature\n\n### Testing Strategy\n- Unit tests for managers and business logic\n- UI tests for critical user flows\n- Test on multiple device types (iPhone, iPad)\n- Verify location permission flows\n\n### Debugging Tips\n- Use Xcode's location simulation for testing\n- Monitor battery usage during development\n- Test background/foreground transitions\n- Verify privacy compliance\n - Test deep links: &#96;miataru://&lt;DEVICE_ID&gt;&#96; (Simulator: &#96;xcrun simctl openurl booted miataru://ABCDEF...&#96;)\n\n## Common Development Tasks\n\n### Adding New Features\n1. Create view in appropriate platform folder\n2. Add manager if business logic is needed\n3. Update settings if user preferences are involved\n4. Add localization strings\n5. Test on all target platforms\n\n### Location Permission Handling\n- Always check authorization status before requesting\n- Provide clear user feedback\n- Handle denied permissions gracefully\n- Respect user's privacy choices\n\n### Settings Management\n- Use &#96;SettingsManager&#96; for all user preferences\n- Observe changes and update UI accordingly\n- Provide sensible defaults\n- Validate user input\n - Register defaults from &#96;Settings.bundle/Root.plist&#96; via &#96;SettingsManager.registerDefaultsFromSettingsBundle()&#96;",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "- Stores &amp; caches:",

          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving to Application Support)",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; (last locations + reverse geocode queue)",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "  - &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; (cached &#96;MKRoute&#96; by device &amp; transport; distance-based validity)",
            "lineNumber": 45

        "contents": "- Data &amp; Caching:\n  - &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, &#96;DeviceGroupStore&#96; (secure archiving under Application Support)\n  - &#96;DeviceLocationCacheStore&#96; (latest device locations + reverse geocoded placemarks)\n  - &#96;RouteCacheStore&#96; (cached routes keyed by device/transport; distance threshold validation)\n- Utilities:\n  - &#96;thisDeviceIDManager&#96; (device ID generation + legacy migration)\n  - &#96;Haptic&#96; (feedback utilities)\n\n## 🔑 Key Features\n\n### Location Management\n- **Privacy-First**: User controls all location sharing\n- **Battery Optimized**: High-accuracy foreground; significant-change background\n- **Permission Handling**: Staged requests (WhenInUse → Always when opted-in)\n- **Background Support**: Significant-change updates\n\n### Device Management\n- **Multi-Device**: Track multiple devices\n- **Group Support**: Organize devices into groups\n- **QR Code Sharing**: Share own device, scan to add others\n- **Deep Link**: &#96;miataru://&lt;DEVICE_ID&gt;&#96; adds devices via sheet\n\n### User Experience\n- **Onboarding Flow**: Guided setup (iPhone/iPad-optimized)\n- **Settings Control**: Comprehensive preferences via SettingsManager\n- **Error Handling**: Transient overlays\n- **Localization**: German, English, and Japanese\n\n## 📱 Platform-Specific Considerations\n\n### iPhone\n- Touch-optimized interface\n- Location permission workflows\n- Deep-link and QR onboarding\n- Battery optimization features\n\n### iPad\n- Larger screen layouts\n- Split view support\n- Enhanced device management\n- Optimized for productivity\n\n### Mac\n- Not currently targeted (Mac directory hosts onboarding previews only)\n\n## 🛠️ Development Guidelines\n\n### Code Organization\n- **Views**: Minimal UI logic, delegate to managers\n- **Managers**: Handle business logic and data\n- **Models**: Use SwiftUI data binding\n- **Assets**: Organized by platform and feature\n\n### State Management\n- Use ObservableObject for view models\n- Implement proper MVVM pattern\n- Handle app lifecycle changes\n- Manage user preferences reactively\n\n### Testing Strategy\n- Unit tests for business logic\n- UI tests for critical flows",

        },
        "contents": "# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\n\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\n\n## App Navigation and Views\n**For users:**\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\n\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;iPhone_RootView&#96; constructs the &#96;TabView&#96; and hosts &#96;iPhone_DevicesView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_GroupsView&#96;, &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, and &#96;iPhone_SettingsView&#96;.\n- &#96;MiataruRootView&#96; selects platform‑specific root containers so iPad and Mac can embed their own navigation styles.\n- iPad supports opening device detail windows using a value‑based &#96;WindowGroup(for: String)&#96; and context menu/drag interactions.\n\n## Location Tracking\n**For users:**\n- Enable background and foreground tracking in *Settings* to share your location with a Miataru server.\n- The app sends updates even with the screen locked and records a log of recent updates.\n- Location sharing can store history on the server and works offline until network connectivity resumes.\n- Tracking accuracy, activity type, and sensitivity are configurable in *Settings*, and a \"Location Tracking Details\" page shows the last GPS and server updates.\n\n- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\n- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\n\n**For developers:**\n- &#96;LocationManager&#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &#96;MiataruAPIClient&#96;.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

                  "lineNumber": 9229,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\n\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &amp;#96;QRCode&amp;#96; package and supports &amp;#96;ShareLink&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;MFMailComposeViewController&amp;#96;.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; validates the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\n\\n## Onboarding Flow\\n**For users:**\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launc [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\\n- Low Power Mode and scene phase changes are observed (e.g., &amp;#96;Notification.Name.NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange&amp;#96;) to gate animations like shimmer/pulsing without changing data behavior.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_LocationStatusView&amp;#96; renders &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; diagnostics, while &amp;#96;SettingsManager&amp;#96; bindings immediately adjust &amp;#96;CLLocationManager&amp;#96; configuration.\\n\\n## Device Management\\n**For users:** [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"   Damit iOS deine App öffnen kann, wenn ein QR-Code mit einem Link wie &amp;#96;miataru://...&amp;#96; gescannt wird, musst du das URL-Schema &amp;#96;miataru&amp;#96; in deiner App registrieren.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8083,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; integrates &amp;#96;CodeScanner&amp;#96; to scan &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; QR codes, offers a color picker, and prevents duplicate IDs.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8721,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\n\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &amp;#96;QRCode&amp;#96; package and supports &amp;#96;ShareLink&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;MFMailComposeViewController&amp;#96;.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; validates the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\n\\n## Onboarding Flow\\n**For users:**\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launc [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8751,

                }

                  "lineNumber": 11731,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Visual effects such as pulsing accuracy circles and shimmering indicators pause automatically in Low Power Mode or while the app is in the background.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\\n- Low Power Mode and scene phase changes are observed (e.g., &amp;#96;Notification.Name.NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange&amp;#96;) to gate animations like shimmer/pulsing without changing data behavior.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_LocationStatusView&amp;#96; renders &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; diagnostics, while &amp;#96;SettingsManager&amp;#96; bindings immediately adjust &amp;#96;CLLocationManager&amp;#96; configuration.\\n\\n## Device Management\\n**For users:** [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "content": "  \"plan\": \"# Implementation Plan: Mutual Navigation and Visitor History\\n\\n## Overview\\n\\nThis plan implements two features:\\n- **A) Mutual Navigation UI**: Detects when both devices are navigating to each other and shows visual indicators\\n- **B) Visitor History UI**: Lists devices that have accessed our location, with ability to add unknown devices\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\n### A) Mutual Navigation Detection\\n\\n**Components:**\\n1. &amp;#96;MutualNavigationDetector&amp;#96;: ObservableObject that manages mutual navigation state\\n   - Polls &amp;#96;GetVisitorHistory&amp;#96; every 15-30s while navigation is active\\n   - Implements hysteresis logic (T_enter=60s, T_exit=90s)\\n   - Caches visitor history to avoid unnecessary UI updates\\n\\n2. Integration in &amp;#96;iPhone_DeviceNavigationView&amp;#96;:\\n   - Track navigation active state (view is visible and polling)\\n   - Use &amp;#96;MutualNavigationDetector&amp;#96; to check if target device appears in visitor history\\n   - Update UI when mutual state changes\\n\\n**Files [... omitted end of long line]"

                  "lineNumber": 28897,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Add other devices by scanning their Miataru QR code.\\n- The QR tab offers one‑tap sharing, and the add‑device sheet guides scanning and rejects non‑Miataru codes.\\n\\n- The share sheet includes additional options, and email sharing attaches the QR image reliably.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&amp;#96; renders customizable QR codes using the &amp;#96;QRCode&amp;#96; package and supports &amp;#96;ShareLink&amp;#96; and &amp;#96;MFMailComposeViewController&amp;#96;.\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_AddDeviceView&amp;#96; validates the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; prefix from scanned codes before accepting an ID and allows manual entry with color selection.\\n\\n## Onboarding Flow\\n**For users:**\\n- A six‑step wizard guides through welcome, permissions, server URL, history settings, personal QR code display, and completion.\\n- Each step shows illustrations and contextual explanations; server selection validates custom HTTPS URLs, and completion flag controls whether the wizard reappears on next launc [... omitted end of long line]"

                {
                  "lineNumber": 302,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"This update in &amp;#96;miataru/miataruApp.swift&amp;#96; adds deep link capture via the AppDelegate using a &amp;#96;PassthroughSubject&amp;#96; and a new &amp;#96;handleIncomingURL&amp;#96; method to ensure URLs are processed even on cold start before the UI fully loads. It includes additions of &amp;#96;application:didFinishLaunching&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;configurationForConnecting&amp;#96;, and &amp;#96;application:open&amp;#96; to forward deep link handling properly. The app now triggers on &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; URLs on reopen via &amp;#96;onOpenURL&amp;#96; combined with an &amp;#96;onReceive&amp;#96; sharing logic. No new user-facing strings were added.\""
                },

                },
                {

                  "lineNumber": 898,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I need to modify the second &amp;#96;WindowGroup&amp;#96; so that it only responds to the URL scheme \\\"miataru\\\" and the path \\\"device\\\" or something similar. Currently, our &amp;#96;onOpenURL&amp;#96; uses the scheme &amp;#96;miataru://{deviceID}&amp;#96; without a path. For &amp;#96;.handlesExternalEvents&amp;#96;, it looks like the matching primarily involves URL hosts. Although we disable restoration to prevent automatic creation, I wonder if making the second group &amp;#96;providesDefaultScene: false&amp;#96; would help. Since we want the MiataruRootView on iPad but don't want the second group auto-creating, I'll check the codebase for any &amp;#96;openWindow&amp;#96; usages.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 907,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"On iPad and macOS, there are APIs that support opening a new window via drag-and-drop, possibly using &amp;#96;.onContinueUserActivity&amp;#96;. One option could be to create a drag preview with a URL like \\\"miataru://DEVICEID\\\". This would allow dropping onto the Dock to open a new window by handling onOpenURL, leading to an \\\"add device\\\" sheet. However, I’m uncertain if the OS will create a new window automatically when dropped onto the app icon. Under macOS, this will trigger application(_:openFile:), but iOS and iPadOS might handle it differently. The user specifically wants to drag out of the device list to create a new window, which indicates that I should prioritize facilitating that outside drag functionality.\""

                  "lineNumber": 974,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I’m thinking it’s essential to ensure we follow localization rules by using &amp;#96;NSLocalizedString&amp;#96; for user-facing strings.                 },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 978,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I see that ShareLink only has one item, but we can combine text that includes a custom scheme and a fallback HTTPS link to the website.                   "lineNumber": 982,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Without control over the website, I might consider sharing both an https link to miataru.com and the miataru:// scheme.                   "lineNumber": 986,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"So, it seems we've changed the code to reuse the email body, which probably includes an explanation.                   "content": "                  \"content\": \"Füge das URL-Handling für miataru:// URLs hinzu.                   "lineNumber": 1344,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"  \\\"contentsAfterEdit\\\": \\\"---\\\\nname: Miataru iOS Widgets\\\\noverview: \\\\\\\"Add a WidgetKit extension with two widget types: a text-based location widget showing device location and distance, and a map snapshot widget showing a rendered map image. Both widgets will support multiple sizes and use App Groups for shared data access.\\\\\\\"\\\\ntodos:\\\\n  - id: shared-data\\\\n    content: Create SharedWidgetData.swift with Codable models and App Group file manager\\\\n    status: pending\\\\n  - id: app-group-sync\\\\n    content: Update DeviceLocationCacheStore and KnownDeviceStore to sync to App Group\\\\n    status: pending\\\\n  - id: map-snapshot\\\\n    content: Create WidgetMapSnapshotGenerator for pre-rendering map images with markers\\\\n    status: pending\\\\n  - id: widget-extension\\\\n    content: Create miataruWidgets extension target with bundle entry point\\\\n    status: pending\\\\n  - id: text-widget\\\\n    content: Implement DeviceLocationTextWidget with small, medium, [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1446,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"On iPad and macOS, there are APIs that support opening a new window via drag-and-drop, possibly using &amp;#96;.onContinueUserActivity&amp;#96;. One option could be to create a drag preview with a URL like \\\"miataru://DEVICEID\\\". This would allow dropping onto the Dock to open a new window by handling onOpenURL, leading to an \\\"add device\\\" sheet. However, I’m uncertain if the OS will create a new window automatically when dropped onto the app icon. Under macOS, this will trigger application(_:openFile:), but iOS and iPadOS might handle it differently. The user specifically wants to drag out of the device list to create a new window, which indicates that I should prioritize facilitating that outside drag functionality.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1619,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"it seems that, when i tap on a widget it opens the app with the miataru:// url scheme, handing over a device id. When I left the app (swiping home) previously on a device map the app will still restore that device and not display the device that was handed over when opened through the deeplink URL.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1627,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"Investigating deeplink handling and device map restoration. Searching for where the &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;#96; URL scheme is handled and where the device map view is restored.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 2426,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I need to modify the second &amp;#96;WindowGroup&amp;#96; so that it only responds to the URL scheme \\\"miataru\\\" and the path \\\"device\\\" or something similar. Currently, our &amp;#96;onOpenURL&amp;#96; uses the scheme &amp;#96;miataru://{deviceID}&amp;#96; without a path. For &amp;#96;.handlesExternalEvents&amp;#96;, it looks like the matching primarily involves URL hosts. Although we disable restoration to prevent automatic creation, I wonder if making the second group &amp;#96;providesDefaultScene: false&amp;#96; would help. Since we want the MiataruRootView on iPad but don't want the second group auto-creating, I'll check the codebase for any &amp;#96;openWindow&amp;#96; usages.&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/think&amp;gt;\""
                },

                  "content": "- [x] Identify why miataru:// URL device not opened on reopen state"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1144,
                  "content": "This update in &#96;miataru/miataruApp.swift&#96; adds deep link capture via the AppDelegate using a &#96;PassthroughSubject&#96; and a new &#96;handleIncomingURL&#96; method to ensure URLs are processed even on cold start before the UI fully loads. It includes additions of &#96;application:didFinishLaunching&#96;, &#96;configurationForConnecting&#96;, and &#96;application:open&#96; to forward deep link handling properly. The app now triggers on &#96;miataru://&#96; URLs on reopen via &#96;onOpenURL&#96; combined with an &#96;onReceive&#96; sharing logic. No new user-facing strings were added."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1147,
                  "content": "- Test cold start with deep link by launching &#96;xcrun simctl openurl booted miataru://somepath&#96; in the simulator."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1198,
                  "content": "Added a centralized deep-link pipeline so &#96;miataru://&#96; URLs are handled even on cold start before the UI auto-reopens the last map. AppDelegate now captures launch/scene/open events and forwards URLs via a subject, and both &#96;.onOpenURL&#96; and the new handler reuse the same logic to open existing devices or present the add-device sheet."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 1231,

                }
              ]

                  "lineNumber": 653,
                  "content": "        \"diffString\": \"  ### 4. Text Widget (DeviceLocationTextWidget)\\n  \\n- Shows: \\\"Device XYZ is in Locality, Country - X km away\\\"**Supported sizes**:\\n+ Shows: \\\"Device XYZ is in Locality, Country - X km away\\\"**Tap action**: &amp;#96;widgetURL&amp;#96; deep link to &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;lt;deviceID&amp;gt;&amp;#96; to open that device in the app.**Supported sizes**:\\n  \\n  - &amp;#96;.systemSmall&amp;#96; - Device name + location + distance\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 662,
                  "content": "        \"diffString\": \"  - Widget displays cached image with text overlay\\n  \\n- **Supported sizes**:\\n+ **Tap action**: &amp;#96;widgetURL&amp;#96; deep link to &amp;#96;miataru://&amp;lt;deviceID&amp;gt;&amp;#96; to open that device in the app.**Supported sizes**:\\n  \\n  - &amp;#96;.systemSmall&amp;#96; - Map only with marker\","

                  "lineNumber": 683,
                  "content": "  \"contentsAfterEdit\": \"---\\nname: Miataru iOS Widgets\\noverview: \\\"Add a WidgetKit extension with two widget types: a text-based location widget showing device location and distance, and a map snapshot widget showing a rendered map image.               "matches": [
                {
                  "lineNumber": 184,
                  "content": "I need to modify the second &#96;WindowGroup&#96; so that it only responds to the URL scheme \"miataru\" and the path \"device\" or something similar. Currently, our &#96;onOpenURL&#96; uses the scheme &#96;miataru://{deviceID}&#96; without a path. For &#96;.handlesExternalEvents&#96;, it looks like the matching primarily involves URL hosts. Although we disable restoration to prevent automatic creation, I wonder if making the second group &#96;providesDefaultScene: false&#96; would help. Since we want the MiataruRootView on iPad but don't want the second group auto-creating, I'll check the codebase for any &#96;openWindow&#96; usages.&lt;/details&gt;&lt;/think&gt;"
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "file": "./.specstory/history/2025-08-28_07-37Z-kontextmenü-nur-für-gültige-standorte.md",
              "matches": [
                {
                  "lineNumber": 299,
                  "content": "On iPad and macOS, there are APIs that support opening a new window via drag-and-drop, possibly using &#96;.onContinueUserActivity&#96;. One option could be to create a drag preview with a URL like \"miataru://DEVICEID\". This would allow dropping onto the Dock to open a new window by handling onOpenURL, leading to an \"add device\" sheet. However, I’m uncertain if the OS will create a new window automatically when dropped onto the app icon. Under macOS, this will trigger application(_:openFile:), but iOS and iPadOS might handle it differently. The user specifically wants to drag out of the device list to create a new window, which indicates that I should prioritize facilitating that outside drag functionality."
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              "file": "./.specstory/history/2025-08-26_13-18Z-buttons-and-layout-adjustments-for-ui.md",

        "contents": "    func remove(atOffsets offsets: IndexSet) {\n        // Get device IDs that will be removed\n        let deviceIDsToRemove = offsets.map { devices[$0].DeviceID }\n        \n        // Remove devices from the list\n        devices.remove(atOffsets: offsets)\n        \n        // Remove devices from all groups\n        removeDevicesFromAllGroups(deviceIDs: deviceIDsToRemove)\n        \n        save()\n    }\n    \n    func removeDevice(byID deviceID: String) {\n        // Remove device from the list\n        devices.removeAll { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }\n        \n        // Remove device from all groups\n        removeDevicesFromAllGroups(deviceIDs: [deviceID])\n        \n        save()\n    }\n    \n    private func removeDevicesFromAllGroups(deviceIDs: [String]) {\n        let groupStore = DeviceGroupStore.shared\n        \n        for group in groupStore.groups {\n            var changed = false\n            for deviceID in deviceIDs {\n                if group.deviceIDs.contains(deviceID) {\n                    group.removeDevice(deviceID)\n                    changed = true\n                }\n            }\n            if changed {\n                group.objectWillChange.send()\n            }\n        }\n    }\n} ",

        "contents": "        }\n    }\n    \n    private func nearbyDevices(around deviceID: String, coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D, thresholdMeters: Double = 35) -&gt; [KnownDevice] {\n        let targetLocation = CLLocation(latitude: coordinate.latitude, longitude: coordinate.longitude)\n        let devicesWithCoordinates: [(KnownDevice, CLLocationCoordinate2D)] = deviceStore.devices.compactMap { known in\n            if let cached = cachedDeviceCoordinates[known.DeviceID] {\n                return (known, cached)\n            }\n            guard let coord = deviceCoordinate(for: known.DeviceID) else { return nil }\n            return (known, coord)\n        }\n        \n        let closeDevices = devicesWithCoordinates.filter { pair in\n            let loc = CLLocation(latitude: pair.1.latitude, longitude: pair.1.longitude)\n            return targetLocation.distance(from: loc) &lt;= thresholdMeters\n        }.map { $0.0 }\n        \n        let tapped = closeDevices.first(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID })\n        let others = closeDevices.filter { $0.DeviceID != deviceID }\n            .sorted { $0.DeviceName.localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare($1.DeviceName) == .orderedAscending }\n        \n        if let tapped {\n            return [tapped] + others\n        }\n        return others\n    }\n    \n    private func deviceCoordinate(for deviceID: String) -&gt; CLLocationCoordinate2D?         "contents": "/*\n * Copyright (c) 2013-2025, Daniel Kirstenpfad, www.miataru.com\n *\n * DeviceGroup.swift\n * miataru\n *\n * Created by Daniel Kirstenpfad on 20.06.25.\n */\n\nimport Foundation\nimport UIKit\nimport Combine\n\n@objc(DeviceGroup)\nclass DeviceGroup: NSObject, ObservableObject, NSCoding, NSSecureCoding, Identifiable {\n    @Published @objc var groupName: String {\n        didSet {\n            objectWillChange.send()\n        }\n    }\n    @Published @objc var deviceIDs: Set&lt;String&gt; = [] {\n        didSet {\n            objectWillChange.send()\n        }\n    }\n    @Published @objc var groupPosition: Int = 0 {\n        didSet {\n            objectWillChange.send()\n        }\n    }\n    \n    var id: String { groupName }\n    \n    init(name: String) {\n        self.groupName = name\n    }\n    \n    required init?(coder aDecoder: NSCoder) {\n        self.groupName = aDecoder.decodeObject(forKey: \"groupName\") as? String ?? \"\"\n        if let deviceIDsArray = aDecoder.decodeObject(forKey: \"deviceIDs\") as? [String] {\n            self.deviceIDs = Set(deviceIDsArray)\n        }\n        self.groupPosition = aDecoder.decodeInteger(forKey: \"groupPosition\")\n    }\n    \n    func encode(with aCoder: NSCoder) {\n        aCoder.encode(groupName, forKey: \"groupName\")\n        aCoder.encode(Array(deviceIDs), forKey: \"deviceIDs\")\n        aCoder.encode(groupPosition, forKey: \"groupPosition\")\n    }\n    \n    static var supportsSecureCoding: Bool {\n        return true\n    }\n    \n    func addDevice(_ deviceID: String) {\n        deviceIDs.insert(deviceID)\n    }\n    \n    func removeDevice(_ deviceID: String) {\n        deviceIDs.remove(deviceID)\n    }\n    \n    func containsDevice(_ deviceID: String) -&gt; Bool {\n        return deviceIDs.contains(deviceID)\n    }\n    \n    func toggleDevice(_ deviceID: String) {\n        if containsDevice(deviceID) {\n            removeDevice(deviceID)\n        } else {\n            addDevice(deviceID)\n        }\n    }\n} ",

        "contents": "    private func isCoordinate(_ coordinate: CLLocationCoordinate2D, inside region: MKCoordinateRegion) -&gt; Bool {\n        let halfLat = region.span.latitudeDelta / 2.0\n        let halfLon = region.span.longitudeDelta / 2.0\n        // Latitude simple bounds\n        let latOk = abs(coordinate.latitude - region.center.latitude) &lt;= halfLat\n        // Longitude shortest-arc difference (wrap-around at +/-180)\n        func shortestLongitudeDelta(_ lon1: Double, _ lon2: Double) -&gt; Double {\n            var delta = lon1 - lon2\n            while delta &gt; 180 { delta -= 360 }\n            while delta &lt; -180 { delta += 360 }\n            return delta\n        }\n        let lonDelta = abs(shortestLongitudeDelta(coordinate.longitude, region.center.longitude))\n        let lonOk = lonDelta &lt;= halfLon || region.span.longitudeDelta &gt;= 360\n        return latOk &amp;&amp; lonOk\n    }\n    \n    // Computed property to get the current device from the store\n    private var device: KnownDevice? {\n        deviceStore.devices.first { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }\n    }\n    \n    private var selectedActionDevice: KnownDevice? {\n        deviceStore.devices.first { $0.DeviceID == (selectedActionDeviceID ?? deviceID) }\n    }\n    \n    // Computed property to get the best available location for map initialization\n    private var bestAvailableLocation: CLLocationCoordinate2D {\n        // First priority: Device location (if available)",

        "contents": "        }\n        return nil\n    }\n    \n    private func computeNearbyGroups(from coords: [String: CLLocationCoordinate2D], thresholdMeters: Double = 35) -&gt; [String: [KnownDevice]] {\n        var result: [String: [KnownDevice]] = [:]\n        let deviceLookup = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: deviceStore.devices.map { ($0.DeviceID, $0) })\n        \n        for (id, coord) in coords {\n            let targetLocation = CLLocation(latitude: coord.latitude, longitude: coord.longitude)\n            var nearbyIDs: [String] = []\n            for (otherID, otherCoord) in coords {\n                guard otherID != id else { continue }\n                let loc = CLLocation(latitude: otherCoord.latitude, longitude: otherCoord.longitude)\n                if targetLocation.distance(from: loc) &lt;= thresholdMeters {\n                    nearbyIDs.append(otherID)\n                }\n            }\n            guard !nearbyIDs.isEmpty else { continue }\n            let ordered = ([id] + nearbyIDs.sorted { (deviceLookup[$0]?.DeviceName ?? $0)\n                .localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare(deviceLookup[$1]?.DeviceName ?? $1) == .orderedAscending })\n                .compactMap { deviceLookup[$0] }\n            if ordered.count &gt; 1 {\n                result[id] = ordered\n            }\n        }\n        return result\n    }\n\n    // Preloads history before navigating to the dedicated history map to avoid switching views when no data exists.\n    private func preloadHistoryAndNavigate(for device: KnownDevice) {\n        guard !isHistoryPreloading else { return }\n        isHistoryPreloading = true\n        Task {\n            await fetchHistoryBeforeNavigation(for: device)\n            await MainActor.run {\n                isHistoryPreloading = false\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Fetches history and navigates only when entries are available. Shows an overlay on the current map if empty or failed.\n    private func fetchHistoryBeforeNavigation(for device: KnownDevice) async {\n\n        // Prefer cached history; do not navigate if cache is empty.",

Fix complete. The issue was on line 121 of `miataruApp.swift`: the code called `.uppercased()` on the deviceID extracted from the deep link URL.

**What was wrong:**
- The code was converting `"Amsterdam_nl"` to `"AMSTERDAM_NL"` 
- But deviceIDs are case-sensitive, so this broke the matching

**The fix:**
- Removed the `.uppercased()` call
- The deviceID now preserves its original case from the URL

Deep links like `miataru://Amsterdam_nl` will now work correctly with case-sensitive deviceIDs. The comparison `$0.DeviceID == deviceID` in the code will match the exact case as stored.
